messages:
lucas_support: Hey billing + finance — customer acct `acct_8X4` (Acme Integrations) says their Feb invoice is ~38k tokens higher than the dashboard export. They pointed at a recurring spike right at midnight PST each day. Invoice id: inv_2026_02_72. Can someone triage?

sara_billing: Thanks. Do we have the raw invoice line items and the dashboard CSV they exported? Also: did they change plans mid-month?

lucas_support: Attached CSV from customer (pasted below). They did change from Standard -> Pro on Feb 15 at ~00:30 PST. Invoice lines show full Pro unit rate for 15th and onward, dashboard shows a partial-day proration. Customer sees a total mismatch.

jordan_finance: Quick note — our billing cutoff window is midnight UTC for metering -> invoice batching. The dashboard per-day view is rendered in the account timezone (their org set to America/Los_Angeles). That can create 1-day offsets for events near 00:00 local. Could explain some drift, but 38k tokens sounds bigger than timezone alone. :thinking_face:

anya_eng: Can you dump the metering events around the midnight boundaries? Specifically: token events for acct_8X4 from 2026-02-14 23:30 UTC -> 2026-02-16 08:00 UTC. Use this query and paste results (date trunc both UTC and America/Los_Angeles):

```sql
SELECT
  date_trunc('day', occurred_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') as utc_day,
  date_trunc('day', occurred_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles') as la_day,
  sum(token_count) as tokens,
  count(*) as rows
FROM metering.events
WHERE account_id = 'acct_8X4'
  AND occurred_at >= '2026-02-14T23:30:00Z'
  AND occurred_at <= '2026-02-16T08:00:00Z'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1;
```

lucas_support: Pasting the customer's dashboard CSV excerpt they sent (trimmed):

```
date, tokens
2026-02-14, 12,234
2026-02-15, 18,512
2026-02-16, 11,002
```

And our invoice lines (summarized) show Feb-15 tokens = 45,000 (Pro rate).

anya_eng: OK looking at the metering dump — there's a repeated pattern: at ~08:00 UTC / 00:00 PST we see a batch of requests that have null idempotency_key + retry_count > 0. Example log row (sanitized):

```
metering.ingest | account=acct_8X4 | token_count=12345 | request_id=null | retries=2 | route=/v1/embeddings
```

Those requests were split by the runtime batching into many internal slices for latency reasons. Dashboard aggregation dedupes using the runtime batch_id when present, but our billing pipeline dedupes only on client idempotency keys. If a client didn't set one, retries and internal split slices got billed multiple times. That can produce the ~38k delta.

jordan_finance: yikes. So two pieces: timezone/proration mismatch + double-counting for requests without idempotency keys. Can we quantify how much is from dedupe failures vs proration?

anya_eng: I ran a quick aggregation: dedupe-failure attributable tokens = ~31,780. Timezone/proration window accounts for the remaining ~6k. So most of it is duplicate counting.

maya_pm: For the plan change: product currently applies proration at UTC day boundary when computing the effective unit rate for invoice lines. The Console uses local-day for the UI, so that 30-min drift (00:30 PST) explains the 6k residual. We'll need to align docs, but that's minor.

jordan_finance: Given the numbers, we should credit the customer for the duplicate-count portion. I'm OK with a provisional credit of the token-equivalent cost for 31,780 tokens while eng implements a fix.

lucas_support: Customer asked for repro steps and ETA for a fix. Any short-term mitigation we can offer?

anya_eng: Short-term mitigation options: 1) run a billing reprocess to remove events that match our dedupe heuristic (same account + timestamp window + null idempotency + retry_count>0) — low-risk, reversible, but needs finance sign-off. 2) patch billing pipeline to dedupe on internal runtime_batch_id when present (longer deploy). For an immediate stopgap, we can add a 48-hour dedupe window for events lacking idempotency_key — that'll prevent further duplicates being billed while we roll the proper patch. ETA: runway ~48-72h for the stopgap plus monitoring. Full fix ~1-2 weeks.

jordan_finance: Approve provisional credit and billing reprocess if eng provides a vetted list of event IDs to drop. I'll prepare a customer-facing note: mention we found duplicate counting from retries and timezone proration edge. I'll hold off final credit until we push the stopgap and confirm no other accounts impacted.

lucas_support: I'll update the customer: provisional credit being prepared, ETA 48-72h for stopgap, full fix in ~2 weeks, and offer a temporary invoice hold for the disputed lines. Thanks everyone. :pray:

anya_eng: One more helpful command (internal) to pull the suspect events for review:

```
curl -s "https://metrics.internal.api/events?account=acct_8X4&from=2026-02-15T00:00:00Z&to=2026-02-16T00:00:00Z&filter=null_idempotency=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN"
```

jordan_finance: I'll wait for that payload and then draft the credit memo. Good catch.

lucas_support: Filed follow-up ticket in CS queue with links to this thread and requested artifacts. I'll ping once we have the repro list.
